text: Transport Minister Chris Bishop confirmed the Government will retain a Clean Vehicle Standard for new and used vehicle imports, following a review of its settings.

Chris Hipkins unveiled the final stage of Labour's Small Business Action Plan in Rotorua, including a $2m annual AI small-business fund, an expanded AI Advisory pilot, and a boost to the Founder and Startup Support Programme.
Announced a plan to cut the number of government departments from 43 to 19, alongside new welfare policy framed around personal responsibility and the value of paid work.
Announced a policy to restrict general-election voting to NZ citizens, removing the current right of some non-citizen permanent residents to vote after 12 months' residence.

Co-leader Chlöe Swarbrick and MP Ricardo Menéndez March announced a Member's Bill, the Commerce (Excessive Pricing in Retail Grocery Industry) Amendment Bill, aiming to make it illegal for supermarkets to charge unreasonably high grocery prices.

Criticised the Government's reported plan to scrap existing Mana Whakahono ā Rohe iwi–council partnership agreements as part of planning-law reform, calling it a step back from honouring Te Tiriti at the local level.
Announced further South Island candidates, saying they reflect workers who understand the cost-of-living crisis and want a change of government and direction.
